words.enDefinition: the process of arranging roles and relationships across an organisation

examples.en: Our lecturer introduced organisational design with a case about a repair business that had just doubled in size.
examples.zh: 讲师用一家规模刚翻倍的维修企业作为案例，介绍「组织设计」。

examples.en: The class compared approaches to organisational design before deciding how to group the library service teams.
examples.zh: 同学们先比较了不同的「组织设计」做法，再决定怎样给图书馆服务团队分组。

words.enDefinition: the arrangement of roles and authority within an organisation

examples.en: The organisational structure showed which teams reported directly to the manager of the arts centre.
examples.zh: 该「组织结构」显示哪些团队直接向艺术中心经理汇报。

examples.en: Our case report described how the organisational structure changed when the second branch opened.
examples.zh: 我们的案例报告介绍了第二家分店开业后，「组织结构」有什么变化。

words.enDefinition: a diagram of roles and reporting relationships in an organisation

examples.en: The tutor asked us to update the organisational chart after the two departments were combined.
examples.zh: 两个部门合并后，导师让我们更新「组织结构图」。

examples.en: I checked the organisational chart to see where the university print service sat within the department.
examples.zh: 我查看了「组织结构图」，想知道学校的打印业务在这个部门中归哪一级管理。

words.enDefinition: the officially established roles and relationships used to organise work

examples.en: In the formal structure, the project leads report directly to the director of the student enterprise.
examples.zh: 按「正式组织结构」，项目负责人直接向学生企业的负责人汇报。

examples.en: The case described a formal structure that gave local offices responsibility for their own purchases.
examples.zh: 案例中的「正式组织结构」允许当地办事处自行负责采购。

words.enDefinition: the unofficial relationships through which people share information and work together

examples.en: The informal organisation included people from different departments who helped one another with common problems.
examples.zh: 「非正式组织关系」把来自不同部门、会互相帮着解决常见问题的人连在一起。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the informal organisation affected decisions in a small campus publishing team.
examples.zh: 导师问，「非正式组织关系」怎样影响一个小型校园出版团队的决策。

collocations: the role of the informal organisation

words.enDefinition: the extent to which written rules govern how work is done

examples.en: Formalisation increased when the cooperative began writing down rules that had previously been agreed verbally.
examples.zh: 合作社开始把原先口头商定的规则写下来后，「组织正式化」程度提高了。

examples.en: The class discussed how much formalisation would help a small design studio work more consistently.
examples.zh: 班上讨论，小型设计工作室做到何种程度的「组织正式化」有助于统一做法。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement that groups people by their work specialism

examples.en: The fictional publisher used a functional structure with separate editorial, finance, and production teams.
examples.zh: 虚构的这家出版社采用「职能型结构」，分别设有编辑、财务和制作团队。

examples.en: Our tutor asked when a functional structure might make it harder for departments to cooperate.
examples.zh: 导师问，在哪些情况下，「职能型结构」可能让部门之间更难合作。

collocations: organise teams in a functional structure

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with separate units for products, regions, or customer groups

examples.en: The case company moved to a divisional structure when it began serving two very different regions.
examples.zh: 开始服务两个差异很大的地区后，案例公司改用了「事业部制结构」。

examples.en: We drew a divisional structure with one division for repairs and another for equipment hire.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「事业部制结构」，一部负责维修，另一部负责设备出租。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with intersecting lines of responsibility, such as departments and projects

examples.en: In the matrix structure, the designer reported to both the design manager and the project lead.
examples.zh: 在「矩阵式结构」下，设计师同时向设计经理和项目负责人汇报。

examples.en: The class compared a matrix structure with separate departments that rarely shared people across projects.
examples.zh: 班上比较了「矩阵式结构」和部门独立运作、很少跨项目调人的安排。

words.enDefinition: a business unit responsible for a product or related group of products

examples.en: The case company gave each product division responsibility for its own product development and service.
examples.zh: 案例公司让每个「产品事业部」负责自己的产品开发和服务。

examples.en: Our group imagined a product division that made reusable packaging for cafés near university campuses.
examples.zh: 我们小组构想了一个给大学附近的咖啡馆制作可重复使用包装的「产品事业部」。

words.enDefinition: a business unit responsible for a particular area

examples.en: Each geographic division could adapt its repair service to local travel distances and working hours.
examples.zh: 各「地区事业部」可以根据当地交通距离和营业时间调整维修服务。

examples.en: The lecturer asked why the company might create a geographic division for its northern branches.
examples.zh: 讲师问，公司为什么可能为北部的分支设立一个「地区事业部」。

collocations: delegate decisions to a geographic division

words.enDefinition: grouping jobs into departments by shared characteristics or responsibilities

examples.en: We discussed departmentalisation by product after reading a case about a campus equipment supplier.
examples.zh: 读过校园设备供应商的案例后，我们讨论了按产品进行「部门划分」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether departmentalisation by location would help the fictional retailer serve local customers.
examples.zh: 讲师问，按地点做「部门划分」能不能让虚构的零售商更好地服务当地顾客。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with relatively few levels of management

examples.en: The small publisher kept a flat structure so editors could speak directly with the director.
examples.zh: 小出版社保留了「扁平组织结构」，编辑可以直接和负责人交流。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a flat structure would still work when the team doubled in size.
examples.zh: 导师问，团队人数翻倍后，「扁平组织结构」能否继续运作。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with many successive levels of management

examples.en: The case showed a tall structure in which a request passed through several management levels.
examples.zh: 案例中的「多层级组织结构」使一项请求要经过好几级管理人员。

examples.en: We used a tall structure for the simulation and compared how quickly each team made decisions.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟中采用了「多层级组织结构」，比较各小组的决策速度。

collocations: a tall structure with several management layers
move away from a tall structure

words.enDefinition: the removal of one or more levels of management

examples.en: The case company considered delayering after finding that routine requests passed through three levels of approval.
examples.zh: 案例公司发现日常申请要经过三级审批，于是考虑「减少管理层级」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether delayering would put too much responsibility on the remaining branch managers.
examples.zh: 我们小组讨论了「减少管理层级」会不会让留下的分店经理承担过多责任。

words.enDefinition: the number of people who report directly to a manager

examples.en: The lecturer calculated the span of control for a manager who supervised eight team leads.
examples.zh: 讲师计算了直接管理八名组长的经理的「管理幅度」。

examples.en: The case compared the span of control in a small shop with that in its main warehouse.
examples.zh: 案例比较了一家小店和它的主仓库的「管理幅度」。

collocations: review a manager's span of control

words.enDefinition: formal power to direct the work of people who report to you

examples.en: The branch manager had line authority over employees assigned to the shop in our case.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例里，分店经理对分配到店里的员工拥有「直线职权」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked who held line authority after the company split its main repair team.
examples.zh: 导师问，公司拆分主维修团队后，由谁行使「直线职权」。

words.enDefinition: authority to advise or support managers in a specialised area

examples.en: The central finance team exercised staff authority by advising each branch on its annual budget.
examples.zh: 中央财务团队行使「参谋职权」，就各分店的年度预算提供建议。

examples.en: The course case gave the training office staff authority to recommend changes to branch procedures.
examples.zh: 课程案例赋予培训处「参谋职权」，可以建议分店调整操作流程。

words.enDefinition: the principle that each worker takes orders from one supervisor

examples.en: The case used unity of command so each technician received instructions from one direct supervisor.
examples.zh: 案例采用「统一指挥原则」，每名技术员只听一位直属主管安排。

examples.en: We discussed how unity of command would work when two departments shared the workshop staff.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了两个部门共用工作坊人员时，该怎样落实「统一指挥原则」。

collocations: the principle of unity of command

words.enDefinition: an arrangement in which someone reports to two managers

examples.en: Under dual reporting, the analyst reported to the finance manager and the campus project director.
examples.zh: 实行「双重汇报」时，分析员要向财务经理和校园项目负责人汇报。

examples.en: The case company tried dual reporting after several teams began sharing the same design staff.
examples.zh: 几个团队开始共用同一批设计人员后，案例公司尝试了「双重汇报」。

words.enDefinition: a secondary reporting relationship, usually with less direct authority

examples.en: The case used dotted-line reporting so a regional lead could advise staff outside her direct team.
examples.zh: 案例采用「虚线汇报关系」，让地区负责人能够指导直属团队以外的员工。

examples.en: Our tutor showed dotted-line reporting between the designer and the project manager on the chart.
examples.zh: 导师在图上标出了设计师和项目经理之间的「虚线汇报关系」。

words.enDefinition: a manager responsible for a specialist department or area

examples.en: The functional manager approved training for designers assigned to several different campus projects that term.
examples.zh: 该「职能部门经理」批准了本学期派往不同校园项目的设计师的培训。

examples.en: I drew the functional manager above the finance team in our organisational design exercise.
examples.zh: 在组织设计练习里，我把「职能部门经理」画在财务团队上方。

words.enDefinition: support functions provided centrally for several parts of an organisation

examples.en: The case company used shared services to handle payroll for all three of its branches.
examples.zh: 案例公司通过「共享服务」处理三个分店的薪资。

examples.en: Our group asked whether shared services would free local managers to concentrate on their customers.
examples.zh: 我们小组想知道，「共享服务」能不能让当地经理腾出精力专注服务顾客。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement that carries out much of its work through teams

examples.en: The course case described a team-based structure where each group handled repairs from booking to collection.
examples.zh: 课程案例中的「团队制结构」让每组都负责从预约到取件的整个维修流程。

examples.en: Under the team-based structure, employees from different specialisms planned each exhibition together from the beginning.
examples.zh: 在「团队制结构」下，不同专业的员工从一开始就共同筹划每场展览。

words.enDefinition: an organisation in which most work is arranged around projects

examples.en: The case described a project-based organisation that assembled a different team for each new exhibition.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了一个「项目制组织」，每场新展览都会另组一支团队。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how staff developed their careers inside a small project-based organisation without fixed departments.
examples.zh: 导师问，在没有固定部门的小型「项目制组织」里，员工怎样发展自己的职业。

words.enDefinition: an organisation coordinated through linked units or partner organisations

examples.en: The textbook case described a network organisation linking a design studio to several independent makers.
examples.zh: 教材案例介绍了一家「网络型组织」，把设计工作室和几家独立制造商连在一起。

examples.en: We discussed how a network organisation might coordinate work when each partner had different schedules.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了每个合作伙伴时间安排不同时，「网络型组织」怎样协调工作。

words.enDefinition: a tightly controlled arrangement with specialised roles and formal rules

examples.en: The fictional warehouse used a mechanistic structure with clearly prescribed duties and several approval levels.
examples.zh: 虚构的这家仓库采用「机械式组织结构」，职责有明确规定，审批分好几级。

examples.en: In the exercise, a mechanistic structure made it easy to see who could approve each change.
examples.zh: 练习中，「机械式组织结构」让每项变更由谁批准变得很清楚。

words.enDefinition: a flexible arrangement with adaptable roles and less central control

examples.en: The design team adopted an organic structure so members could shift roles quickly during the project.
examples.zh: 设计团队采用「有机式组织结构」，成员可以在项目期间迅速改变分工。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how an organic structure might help a business respond quickly to unexpected requests.
examples.zh: 导师问，「有机式组织结构」如何帮助企业迅速应对计划外的请求。

collocations: switch to a more organic structure

words.enDefinition: a group that works in isolation from other groups

examples.en: The inventory team became an organisational silo because it rarely shared changes with the repair desk.
examples.zh: 库存团队很少把变更情况告诉维修台，成了一个「组织孤岛」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what made the finance office an organisational silo in the class case.
examples.zh: 导师问，课堂案例里的财务处为什么会成为「组织孤岛」。

words.enDefinition: organising interdependent work between people in different functions

examples.en: Cross-functional coordination helped the design, finance, and packing teams agree on a date for the change.
examples.zh: 通过「跨职能协调」，设计、财务和打包团队商定了变更日期。

examples.en: The lecturer asked how the new reporting arrangements might affect cross-functional coordination during the busy term.
examples.zh: 讲师问，新的汇报安排会怎样影响繁忙学期的「跨职能协调」。

words.enDefinition: a purposeful change to an existing arrangement of roles or units

examples.en: The fictional retailer began an organisational redesign after opening separate stores for repairs and rentals.
examples.zh: 虚构的零售商为维修和租赁分别开店后，开始「组织重构」。

examples.en: Our group linked the organisational redesign to problems that appeared when the first branch opened.
examples.zh: 我们小组把「组织重构」与第一家分店开业时出现的问题联系起来。

words.enDefinition: part of a larger company with its own strategic focus

examples.en: The textbook company treated equipment leasing as a strategic business unit with its own goals.
examples.zh: 教材案例公司把设备租赁当成一个有自身目标的「战略业务单元」。

examples.en: Our class debated whether the repair service could become a strategic business unit with distinct competitors.
examples.zh: 我们班讨论了维修服务是否可以成为一个面对不同竞争对手的「战略业务单元」。

words.enDefinition: a unit responsible for both the revenues and costs it generates

examples.en: In our simulation, each branch operated as a profit centre and reported its own results.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，每家分店作为「利润中心」运营，并汇报各自的盈亏。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the café could be treated as a profit centre within the university.
examples.zh: 讲师问，咖啡馆能不能被看作学校内部的一个「利润中心」。

collocations: treat a department as a profit centre

words.enDefinition: freedom for a local unit to make its own decisions

examples.en: Greater local autonomy let each branch set opening hours that suited its neighbourhood and staff.
examples.zh: 更大的「下属单位自主权」让每家分店能自行设定适合附近居民和员工的营业时间。

examples.en: The class case asked how much local autonomy the central office should give its stores.
examples.zh: 课堂案例问，总部应该给各家门店多少「下属单位自主权」。

collocations: a high degree of local autonomy

words.enDefinition: placing decision-making authority at higher levels of an organisation

examples.en: Centralisation meant the campus outlets needed head office approval for changes to their price lists.
examples.zh: 「集权化」意味着校园各门店修改价目表前都要总部批准。

examples.en: The class discussed whether centralisation would help the branches use a consistent borrowing policy.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了「集权化」能否帮助各分店采用统一的借用政策。

words.enDefinition: shifting decision-making authority away from the centre to local units

examples.en: Decentralisation gave each workshop more freedom to decide which equipment it should repair first.
examples.zh: 「分权化」让各工作坊能更自主地决定先修哪些设备。

examples.en: In the case, decentralisation helped branch managers respond to problems without waiting for head office.
examples.zh: 案例中的「分权化」让分店经理不必等总部就能应对问题。

words.enDefinition: a person responsible for an allocated budget and its use

examples.en: The budget holder checked whether the repair fund could cover an extra set of tools.
examples.zh: 「预算负责人」核实维修经费能不能负担多买一套工具。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked what information the budget holder should see before approving the workshop purchase.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「预算负责人」在批准工作坊的采购前应当看到哪些信息。

words.enDefinition: power officially passed to another person or unit to act

examples.en: The branch lead used delegated authority to approve the replacement of a broken display table.
examples.zh: 分店负责人用「下放的权限」批准更换坏掉的展示桌。

examples.en: We reviewed delegated authority after both departments assumed they could sign off on the purchase.
examples.zh: 两个部门都认为自己能批准采购后，我们重新核对了「下放的权限」。

words.enDefinition: the point at which a decision needs additional approval

examples.en: In our case, the approval threshold determined which purchases had to go to the director.
examples.zh: 我们的案例按「审批门槛」决定哪些采购必须报负责人批准。

examples.en: The branch exceeded the approval threshold when it ordered a second set of display stands.
examples.zh: 分店订购第二套展示架后，采购金额超过了「审批门槛」。

words.enDefinition: the limits on decisions and actions a person may take

examples.en: The case report described the scope of authority for the manager of the campus bookshop.
examples.zh: 案例报告说明了校园书店经理的「权限范围」。

examples.en: We asked whether changing the opening hours fell within the assistant's scope of authority.
examples.zh: 我们问，调整营业时间是否属于助理的「权限范围」。

collocations: act within the scope of authority

words.enDefinition: the arrangement of bodies and roles that direct and oversee an organisation

examples.en: The students drew the governance structure of a cooperative with a board elected by members.
examples.zh: 学生画出了一个由成员选举董事会的合作社的「治理结构」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the governance structure would change if workers had seats on the board.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果员工能在董事会中占有席位，「治理结构」会发生什么变化。

words.enDefinition: the system by which a company is directed and overseen

examples.en: We studied corporate governance through a case about who could question the founder's decisions.
examples.zh: 我们用一个关于谁有权质疑创始人决策的案例学习「公司治理」。

examples.en: The corporate governance module compared the responsibilities of managers, board members, and company owners.
examples.zh: 「公司治理」课比较了经理、董事会成员和公司所有者的职责。

words.enDefinition: a board's monitoring of management and major activities

examples.en: The case explored how board oversight could improve reporting at a growing student enterprise.
examples.zh: 案例探讨了「董事会监督」如何改善一家发展中学生企业的报告制度。

examples.en: For our presentation, we used a workshop expansion plan to show what board oversight involved.
examples.zh: 我们在展示中用一个工作坊扩建计划说明「董事会监督」包括什么。

words.enDefinition: a group responsible for guiding and overseeing a company

examples.en: In the case, the board of directors reviewed management's plan to open a second branch.
examples.zh: 在案例中，「董事会」审阅了管理层开设第二家分店的计划。

examples.en: The board of directors asked for an update before deciding whether to support the expansion.
examples.zh: 「董事会」在决定是否支持扩张前，要求了解最新情况。

collocations: report to the board of directors
a meeting of the board of directors

words.enDefinition: the separate oversight body in a two-tier company governance system

examples.en: In our case, the supervisory board reviewed management's progress and challenged its plans for expansion.
examples.zh: 案例中，「监督委员会」审查了管理层的工作进展，并对扩张计划提出质疑。

examples.en: The fictional company's supervisory board discussed the proposed change with worker representatives before meeting management.
examples.zh: 这家虚构公司的「监督委员会」在会见管理层前，与员工代表讨论了拟议的变更。

words.enDefinition: the executive board that manages a company in a two-tier governance system

examples.en: The management board presented its proposal for a new repair centre to the supervisory board.
examples.zh: 「管理委员会」向监督董事会提交了增设维修中心的提案。

examples.en: In class, we discussed which day-to-day decisions belonged to the fictional retailer's management board.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论了这家虚构零售商的「管理委员会」负责哪些日常决策。

collocations: a meeting of the management board

words.enDefinition: a group that offers specialist advice to an organisation

examples.en: The student venture asked its advisory board to review the plan for adding evening appointments.
examples.zh: 学生创业团队请「顾问委员会」审阅增设晚间预约的计划。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained why an advisory board might include a former customer and a local supplier.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了为什么「顾问委员会」可能吸纳一位以前的顾客和一家本地供应商。

words.enDefinition: a board member without ties likely to undermine independent judgment

examples.en: In our case, an independent director questioned the proposed purchase from a business owned by a founder.
examples.zh: 案例中，一位「独立董事」质疑向创始人名下的企业采购的提案。

examples.en: We discussed why the fictional company wanted an independent director with experience in community lending.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了这家虚构公司为什么希望聘请有社区借贷经验的「独立董事」。

words.enDefinition: a board member who does not run daily operations

examples.en: A non-executive director asked the manager how the new equipment would improve the repair service.
examples.zh: 一位「非执行董事」问经理，新设备会怎样改善维修服务。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to compare the managing director's work with that of a non-executive director.
examples.zh: 讲师请我们比较总经理和「非执行董事」的工作。

collocations: a non-executive director on the board

words.enDefinition: the person who leads a board and its meetings

examples.en: The board chair gave both branch managers a chance to explain their concerns about the expansion.
examples.zh: 「董事会主席」让两位分店经理都有机会说明他们对扩张的顾虑。

examples.en: In the simulation, the board chair summarised the discussion before asking members for their views.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「董事会主席」先总结讨论，再请成员发表意见。

words.enDefinition: the mix of people and expertise on a board

examples.en: The class considered how board composition might affect decisions about opening a rural branch.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了「董事会成员构成」会怎样影响开设乡村分店的决策。

examples.en: Our report assessed board composition by looking at members' experience in education, finance, and retail.
examples.zh: 报告从成员在教育、金融和零售领域的经历出发，评估了「董事会成员构成」。

words.enDefinition: a smaller group set up by a board for specific work

examples.en: The board committee reviewed the draft budget before the full board discussed the expansion.
examples.zh: 「董事会下设委员会」先审阅预算草案，之后董事会全体成员才讨论扩张。

examples.en: We recommended a board committee to examine the possible effects of moving the repair centre.
examples.zh: 我们建议由一个「董事会下设委员会」研究搬迁维修中心可能带来的影响。

words.enDefinition: a group responsible for reviewing risks and how they are managed

examples.en: The fictional company's risk committee considered what would happen if its main supplier stopped trading.
examples.zh: 这家虚构公司的「风险委员会」考虑了如果主要供应商停止营业会怎么样。

examples.en: The risk committee asked management how quickly it could reopen the campus shop after a closure.
examples.zh: 「风险委员会」问管理层，校园商店停业后能多快重开。

words.enDefinition: one governing board that may include executive and non-executive members

examples.en: The lecturer drew a unitary board with executives and outside directors sitting on the same body.
examples.zh: 讲师画了一个「单层董事会」，高管和外部董事同属一个机构。

examples.en: Our case used a unitary board to review management's plans for expanding the equipment service.
examples.zh: 在案例中，由「单层董事会」审查管理层扩大器材服务的计划。

words.enDefinition: the formal responsibilities and powers assigned to a board

examples.en: The students read the board mandate to see whether the board could approve a new workshop.
examples.zh: 学生查阅了「董事会职责与权限」，想知道董事会能否批准增设工作坊。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether that decision belonged within the board mandate in the fictional case.
examples.zh: 导师问，在虚构案例中，那项决策是否属于「董事会职责与权限」的范围。

words.enDefinition: a written statement defining a group's purpose, scope, and responsibilities

examples.en: We drafted terms of reference for the committee before giving it responsibility for the pilot.
examples.zh: 我们先为委员会拟定「职责范围说明」，再让它负责试点。

examples.en: The terms of reference stated which decisions the working group could make without going back to the board.
examples.zh: 「职责范围说明」明确了哪些决定工作小组可以自行作出，无需再次提请董事会。

words.enDefinition: decisions set aside for approval by a specified person or group

examples.en: Our case placed the sale of a branch on the list of reserved matters for the board.
examples.zh: 案例把出售分店列为董事会的「保留审批事项」。

examples.en: The students checked whether buying a second workshop was one of the board's reserved matters.
examples.zh: 学生查看了购置第二个工作坊是否属于董事会的「保留审批事项」。

collocations: draw up a list of reserved matters

words.enDefinition: arrangements that prevent one person or group from holding unchecked power

examples.en: The students proposed checks and balances so the branch manager could not approve her own expenses.
examples.zh: 学生提出了「制衡机制」，防止分店经理自行批准自己的开支。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked how the checks and balances would work in a small student cooperative.
examples.zh: 讲师问，一个小型学生合作社将怎样运用这套「制衡机制」。

collocations: a system of checks and balances

words.enDefinition: assigning related tasks to different people to keep work independently checked

examples.en: In the case, separation of duties meant one person bought materials and another checked the delivery.
examples.zh: 案例中的「职责分离」是让一人采购材料、另一人验收送货。

examples.en: We discussed separation of duties when designing the checkout process for the campus equipment shop.
examples.zh: 为校园设备店设计结账流程时，我们讨论了「职责分离」。

collocations: a policy on separation of duties

words.enDefinition: a situation where owners and those controlling management are different people

examples.en: Our lecturer used a family business with hired managers to illustrate the separation of ownership and control.
examples.zh: 讲师用聘请职业经理人的家族企业来说明「所有权与控制权分离」。

examples.en: The class discussed how the separation of ownership and control changed who made expansion decisions.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了「所有权与控制权分离」如何改变扩张决策的归属。

collocations: illustrate the separation of ownership and control
consequences of the separation of ownership and control
discuss the separation of ownership and control

words.enDefinition: freedom for managers to make judgments within agreed limits

examples.en: In our case, the shop's weekend opening hours were left to management discretion.
examples.zh: 在案例中，商店周末的营业时间由「管理层自主裁量权」决定。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how management discretion might help the team respond to an unusually busy week.
examples.zh: 导师问，「管理层自主裁量权」怎样帮助团队应对格外忙碌的一周。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement defining who answers for decisions and results

examples.en: We drafted an accountability framework spelling out who would answer for spending at each branch.
examples.zh: 我们起草了一份「问责框架」，明确各家分店的开支由谁负责。

examples.en: The workshop's accountability framework said that managers had to explain major changes to the board.
examples.zh: 工作坊的「问责框架」规定，管理人员得向董事会解释重大变更。

words.enDefinition: arrangements for representing affected groups in decisions

examples.en: The cooperative strengthened stakeholder representation by adding seats for workshop users and local residents.
examples.zh: 合作社增设了工作坊用户和附近居民的席位，加强了「利益相关方代表机制」。

examples.en: The case prompted a discussion about stakeholder representation on the board of a student enterprise.
examples.zh: 案例引发了对学生企业董事会「利益相关方代表机制」的讨论。

words.enDefinition: an approach that involves affected people in guiding an organisation

examples.en: The campus food project tried participatory governance by inviting members to help set its priorities.
examples.zh: 校园餐饮项目尝试「参与式治理」，请成员参与确定先做哪些事。

examples.en: Our class debated whether participatory governance could work when half the members lived off campus.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了一半成员住在校外时，「参与式治理」是否行得通。

words.enDefinition: shared beliefs and habits that shape how an organisation works

examples.en: The guest speaker described an organisational culture where staff were comfortable admitting small mistakes.
examples.zh: 客座讲者描述了一种让员工可以坦然承认小错误的「组织文化」。

examples.en: Our report examined how organisational culture influenced the way the workshop welcomed new members.
examples.zh: 报告分析了「组织文化」怎样影响工作坊接纳新成员的方式。

words.enDefinition: an assessment of how well an organisation is directed and overseen

examples.en: The fictional cooperative began a governance review after members asked for clearer rules about decisions.
examples.zh: 成员希望把决策规则说得更清楚，这家虚构的合作社于是启动了「治理审查」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to show what information a governance review would need from each branch.
examples.zh: 导师让我们说明，「治理审查」需要从各分店收集哪些信息。

collocations: the findings of a governance review

words.enDefinition: choices about the businesses and markets a company operates in

examples.en: Our case examined the corporate strategy behind a publisher's decision to enter the training business.
examples.zh: 我们研究了某出版社决定进入培训行业背后的「公司层战略」。

examples.en: The tutor asked how corporate strategy would change if the retailer sold one of its divisions.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果这家零售商出售一个事业部，「公司层战略」会怎样改变。

words.enDefinition: a plan for succeeding against rivals in a market

examples.en: The fictional repair firm chose a competitive strategy based on fast service rather than broader coverage.
examples.zh: 虚构的维修企业选择以快速服务为主的「竞争战略」，没有把重点放在扩大覆盖面上。

examples.en: In our report, we compared the competitive strategy of a campus bookshop with two online sellers.
examples.zh: 在报告中，我们把校园书店的「竞争战略」和两家网店的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the process of choosing goals and how to pursue them

examples.en: Our tutor used strategy formulation to connect the repair business's goals with its available resources.
examples.zh: 导师通过「战略制定」说明如何把维修企业的目标与可用资源联系起来。

examples.en: The first stage of strategy formulation involved deciding which local markets the case company could serve.
examples.zh: 「战略制定」的第一阶段是决定案例公司能服务哪些本地市场。

words.enDefinition: putting strategic choices into practice across an organisation

examples.en: The lecturer described how strategy execution depended on new training at all three campus outlets.
examples.zh: 讲师介绍了为什么「战略执行」有赖于三个校园门店都开展新的培训。

examples.en: Our group compared the company's announced goals with the actions it took during strategy execution.
examples.zh: 我们小组将公司的公开目标与它在「战略执行」期间采取的行动作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a long-term result an organisation aims to achieve

examples.en: The main strategic objective was to reach more students living far from the main campus.
examples.zh: 主要「战略目标」是服务更多住在主校区较远处的学生。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to state a strategic objective before discussing changes to the workshop.
examples.zh: 导师让我们先提出一个「战略目标」，然后再讨论工作坊该怎么调整。

words.enDefinition: a choice that delivers one benefit while giving up another

examples.en: The case illustrated a strategic trade-off between quick turnaround and a wide range of repair services.
examples.zh: 案例展示了快速交付和提供多种维修服务之间的「战略取舍」。

examples.en: We discussed the strategic trade-off involved in serving only customers within walking distance of campus.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了只服务校园步行范围内的顾客涉及怎样的「战略取舍」。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which activities support one another and the chosen strategy

examples.en: A restricted menu and a single preparation station showed strategic fit in the student café case.
examples.zh: 菜单项目少，并且只设一个备餐工位，这体现了学生咖啡馆案例中的「战略匹配」。

examples.en: Our class looked for strategic fit between the workshop's mobile service and its portable equipment.
examples.zh: 我们观察工作坊推行上门服务和配备便携器材之间的「战略匹配」。

words.enDefinition: the range of markets or customer groups a company chooses to serve

examples.en: The workshop narrowed its competitive scope when it started repairing only bicycles owned by campus staff.
examples.zh: 工作坊开始只修校园员工的自行车后，缩小了「竞争范围」。

examples.en: Our class compared the competitive scope of a neighbourhood café and a regional catering service.
examples.zh: 我们班比较了社区咖啡馆与区域餐饮服务商的「竞争范围」。

words.enDefinition: choices about how to offer distinct value in a market

examples.en: The case examined strategic positioning through a service focused on repairs that could be done overnight.
examples.zh: 案例通过一项专做隔夜修完业务的服务来讨论「战略定位」。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked how the company's strategic positioning would change if it also served large retailers.
examples.zh: 讲师问，如果这家公司也服务大型零售商，它的「战略定位」会怎样改变。

collocations: strategic positioning in a niche market

words.enDefinition: an ability to create more value or operate more efficiently than rivals

examples.en: The student publisher's access to inexpensive campus printing gave it a competitive advantage over local rivals.
examples.zh: 学生出版社能低价使用校园印刷服务，让它相较本地同行有了「竞争优势」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether a faster booking system would create a lasting competitive advantage.
examples.zh: 导师问，更快的预约系统会不会带来长期的「竞争优势」。

words.enDefinition: competing by achieving lower costs than other firms in an industry

examples.en: The case company pursued cost leadership by offering standard repairs and using the same tools everywhere.
examples.zh: 案例公司通过提供标准化维修并在各处使用相同工具追求「成本领先」。

examples.en: We discussed whether cost leadership was possible for a workshop that bought small quantities of materials.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了采购材料量较少的工作坊能否做到「成本领先」。

words.enDefinition: a competitive approach centred on distinct features or benefits

examples.en: The café chose a differentiation strategy based on reliable delivery to buildings outside the main campus.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆选择「差异化战略」，特色是可靠地把餐食送到主校区以外的楼宇。

examples.en: Our instructor asked which parts of the service supported the company's differentiation strategy in the case.
examples.zh: 授课老师问，案例中服务的哪些环节支撑了公司的「差异化战略」。

words.enDefinition: competing by serving a narrow part of a market

examples.en: The case firm adopted a focus strategy by serving campus cycling clubs instead of all riders.
examples.zh: 案例企业采用「聚焦战略」，专做校园骑行社团的生意。

examples.en: The students asked whether a focus strategy made sense for a print shop near two art schools.
examples.zh: 学生问，打印店开在两所艺术院校附近，适不适合采用「聚焦战略」。

words.enDefinition: without a coherent competitive basis after trying incompatible approaches

examples.en: Our lecturer said the fictional cafeteria was stuck in the middle after trying to serve everyone.
examples.zh: 讲师说，虚构的这家食堂想满足所有人，结果「夹在不同战略之间」。

examples.en: The store became stuck in the middle because it offered neither low prices nor a distinctive service.
examples.zh: 这家店价格不低，服务也没有特色，结果「夹在不同战略之间」。

collocations: avoid being stuck in the middle
a company stuck in the middle

words.enDefinition: firms within an industry that follow similar competitive approaches

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the full-service repair shops belonged to a different strategic group from kiosks.
examples.zh: 讲师问，全服务维修店和小修理亭是否属于不同的「战略群组」。

examples.en: Our report placed low-cost textbook sellers in the same strategic group because they offered similar services.
examples.zh: 报告把低价教材卖家放进同一个「战略群组」，因为它们的服务差不多。

words.enDefinition: connected activities through which a company creates and delivers value

examples.en: We mapped the value chain from ordering raw materials to handling repairs after each sale.
examples.zh: 我们画出了从订购原料到售后维修的「价值链」。

examples.en: The case described how a faster packing step changed the value chain for a small publisher.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了更快的打包环节如何改变一家小出版社的「价值链」。

words.enDefinition: a diagram showing how activities reinforce a chosen strategy

examples.en: Our activity system map linked the café's short menu to its quick ordering and preparation steps.
examples.zh: 我们的「活动系统图」把咖啡馆的精简菜单和快速点餐及备餐环节联系起来。

examples.en: The lecturer used an activity system map to show why the mobile repair service travelled light.
examples.zh: 讲师用「活动系统图」说明为什么上门维修服务每次只带少量工具。

words.enDefinition: an organisational strength built through skills that support multiple offerings

examples.en: The case company used its core competence in small-batch printing to serve several very different groups.
examples.zh: 案例公司运用小批量印刷方面的「核心能力」，服务了多个差异很大的群体。

examples.en: Our report asked how the workshop could apply its core competence in repair to another service.
examples.zh: 报告探讨工作坊能否把维修方面的「核心能力」用到另一项服务中。

words.enDefinition: a view of strategy that looks to firm resources for advantage

examples.en: We used the resource-based view to explain the workshop's advantage in repairing unusual equipment quickly.
examples.zh: 我们用「资源基础观」解释这家工作坊为何擅长快速维修少见的设备。

examples.en: The resource-based view helped us discuss how the company's accumulated skills differed from those of rivals.
examples.zh: 「资源基础观」帮我们探讨公司的技能积累与竞争对手有什么不同。

collocations: the resource-based view of the firm

words.enDefinition: a framework for evaluating whether resources are valuable, rare, costly to imitate and supported by the firm's organisation

examples.en: The tutor used the VRIO framework to assess a repair team's unusually deep knowledge of equipment.
examples.zh: 导师用「VRIO 分析框架」评估维修团队对器材掌握的丰富知识。

examples.en: We applied the VRIO framework to assess whether our booking service could give us a lasting advantage.
examples.zh: 我们运用「VRIO 分析框架」评估预约服务能否带来持久优势。

collocations: an assessment using the VRIO framework

words.enDefinition: something that makes entering a market difficult for newcomers

examples.en: In the case, the expensive printing equipment was a barrier to entry for small newcomers.
examples.zh: 在案例中，昂贵的印刷设备是小型新进入者面临的一项「进入壁垒」。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether scarce workshop space created a barrier to entry for local repair services.
examples.zh: 我们班讨论了工坊场地短缺会不会给本地维修服务形成「进入壁垒」。

words.enDefinition: suppliers' ability to influence prices, terms, or availability

examples.en: The bargaining power of suppliers increased when the fictional café lost its only nearby bakery.
examples.zh: 虚构的咖啡馆失去附近唯一一家供货面包坊后，「供应商议价能力」提高了。

examples.en: The group assessed the bargaining power of suppliers before recommending another source of printing paper.
examples.zh: 小组先评估了「供应商议价能力」，再建议另找一家印刷用纸供应商。

collocations: assess the bargaining power of suppliers
changes in the bargaining power of suppliers

words.enDefinition: buyers' ability to demand better prices or other terms

examples.en: The bargaining power of buyers was high because two campus departments placed almost every order.
examples.zh: 两个学校部门下了几乎所有订单，因此「购买方议价能力」很强。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the bargaining power of buyers might change as more repair outlets opened.
examples.zh: 导师问，更多维修门店开业时，「购买方议价能力」可能会怎样变化。

collocations: assess the bargaining power of buyers
changes in the bargaining power of buyers

words.enDefinition: competition among firms already operating in the same industry

examples.en: Competitive rivalry intensified after three nearby repair stalls began offering the same pickup hours.
examples.zh: 附近三个维修摊开始提供相同的自取时间后，「同行竞争」更激烈了。

examples.en: We examined competitive rivalry before discussing whether the campus print shop could charge more.
examples.zh: 在讨论校园打印店能否提价前，我们研究了「同行竞争」。

words.enDefinition: the pressure created by firms that might enter an industry

examples.en: The threat of new entrants increased once cheaper equipment made local badge printing easier.
examples.zh: 设备变便宜，本地印制徽章更容易，「新进入者威胁」也随之增大。

examples.en: The class considered the threat of new entrants even though the repair shop had few rivals.
examples.zh: 尽管维修店的竞争对手不多，班上仍考虑了「新进入者威胁」。

collocations: assess the threat of new entrants
a low threat of new entrants
reduce the threat of new entrants

words.enDefinition: the pressure from alternatives that meet the same need differently

examples.en: The threat of substitutes rose when campus clubs switched from printed notices to electronic screens.
examples.zh: 校园社团把纸质通知改成电子屏之后，「替代品威胁」加大了。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to consider the threat of substitutes for the paid bicycle storage service.
examples.zh: 导师让我们考虑付费自行车寄存服务可能面临的「替代品威胁」。

collocations: respond to the threat of substitutes

words.enDefinition: a framework for analysing five sources of competitive pressure in an industry

examples.en: We applied Porter's Five Forces to compare conditions in local bicycle repair and equipment hire.
examples.zh: 我们运用「波特五力模型」比较本地自行车维修和设备租赁行业的情况。

examples.en: The lecturer used Porter's Five Forces to explain why competition is more than rivalry between shops.
examples.zh: 讲师用「波特五力模型」说明为什么门店间的较量只是竞争的一部分。

collocations: analyse an industry with Porter's Five Forces

words.enDefinition: the expenses or effort involved in moving to another provider

examples.en: The clubs faced switching costs because changing booking tools meant transferring records and training volunteers.
examples.zh: 各社团面临「转换成本」，因为改用其他预约工具意味着要迁移记录并培训志愿者。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which switching costs might matter when the workshop changed suppliers for spare parts.
examples.zh: 导师问，工作坊更换备件供应商时，哪些「转换成本」可能比较重要。

words.enDefinition: a benefit gained by entering a market before competitors

examples.en: The case company gained a first-mover advantage by signing venue agreements before rival services opened.
examples.zh: 案例公司赶在竞争对手开业前签下场地协议，取得了「先发优势」。

examples.en: Our class asked whether the app's first-mover advantage would last once similar services appeared locally.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了本地出现类似服务后，这款应用的「先发优势」还能维持多久。

words.enDefinition: a firm that enters shortly after a pioneer and learns from it

examples.en: The second printing service entered as a fast follower and added pickup hours students had requested.
examples.zh: 第二家打印服务商作为「快速跟随者」入场，增加了学生要求的取货时段。

examples.en: In the simulation, a fast follower could use what the first firm had learned about demand.
examples.zh: 模拟训练中，「快速跟随者」可以利用第一家企业对需求的了解。

words.enDefinition: bringing more stages of the same supply chain under common control

examples.en: In our case, the publisher moved toward vertical integration by bringing previously outsourced printing in-house.
examples.zh: 在案例中，出版社把原先外包的印刷业务收回内部，逐步走向「纵向一体化」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether vertical integration could make paper deliveries less dependent on an outside company.
examples.zh: 导师问，「纵向一体化」能否让纸张配送减少对外部公司的依赖。

words.enDefinition: combining businesses at the same stage of production or distribution

examples.en: We discussed horizontal integration after the fictional campus bookshop agreed to combine with another book retailer.
examples.zh: 虚构的校园书店同意与另一家图书零售商合并后，我们讨论了「横向一体化」。

examples.en: The case showed horizontal integration when two local moving services began operating under the same company.
examples.zh: 案例中，两家本地搬家服务商开始由同一家公司经营，体现了「横向一体化」。

words.enDefinition: expansion into businesses that share resources or capabilities with existing operations

examples.en: The print shop pursued related diversification by adding small design jobs for its existing customers.
examples.zh: 打印店开始为现有顾客接小型设计业务，走的是「相关多元化」路线。

examples.en: In our case, related diversification let the bicycle workshop use the same skills for equipment rentals.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例中，「相关多元化」让自行车工作坊可以把原有技能用到器材租赁上。

words.enDefinition: expansion into businesses with little connection to current operations

examples.en: The case showed unrelated diversification when the repair company bought a small music tutoring service.
examples.zh: 案例中，维修公司收购了一家小型音乐辅导机构，体现了「非相关多元化」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why a publisher might choose unrelated diversification by entering the storage business.
examples.zh: 导师问，一家出版社为什么可能进入仓储业务，走上「非相关多元化」道路。

words.enDefinition: a plan to restore a poorly performing business to viability

examples.en: The case company's turnaround strategy began with reducing losses at the two least busy branches.
examples.zh: 案例公司的「扭转经营困境的战略」从减少两家最清闲分店的亏损做起。

examples.en: Our group proposed a turnaround strategy for a fictional repair chain with declining sales and rising costs.
examples.zh: 我们为一家销量下滑、成本上升的虚构连锁维修企业提出了「扭转经营困境的战略」。

words.enDefinition: a plan for keeping critical services running through a disruption

examples.en: The class drafted a business continuity plan for a print shop that might lose its premises.
examples.zh: 同学们为一家可能失去经营场地的打印店起草了「业务连续性计划」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which student services the business continuity plan would cover during a building closure.
examples.zh: 导师问，大楼关闭期间，「业务连续性计划」会涵盖哪些学生服务。

words.enDefinition: ongoing work to prepare for, withstand, and recover from disruption

examples.en: Business continuity management included checking supplier contacts and reviewing what the team learned from each interruption.
examples.zh: 「业务连续性管理」包括核对供应商的联系方式，并回顾团队从每次中断中学到了什么。

examples.en: The class used a campus library to illustrate business continuity management across several service teams.
examples.zh: 班上用校园图书馆举例，说明怎样让多个服务团队共同开展「业务连续性管理」。

words.enDefinition: an assessment of how disruption would affect operations over time

examples.en: We used a business impact analysis to compare the consequences of losing each workshop for a week.
examples.zh: 我们通过「业务影响分析」，比较各工作坊如果停用一周会分别造成什么后果。

examples.en: The business impact analysis showed that leaving the repair desk closed would delay equipment collection.
examples.zh: 「业务影响分析」显示，维修台继续关闭会让器材领取延迟。

collocations: findings from a business impact analysis

words.enDefinition: an activity essential to keeping an organisation able to operate

examples.en: The case identified equipment collection as a critical business function during the move to another building.
examples.zh: 案例把器材领取列为搬到另一栋楼期间的「关键业务职能」。

examples.en: Our group had to justify why taking bookings was a critical business function for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们小组要说明，对于工作坊来说，接受预约为什么是「关键业务职能」。

words.enDefinition: a resource or service that an important activity relies on

examples.en: Access to the shared kitchen was a critical dependency for the catering project in our case.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例里，能否使用共享厨房是配餐项目的「关键依赖项」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to identify a critical dependency outside the repair team's direct control.
examples.zh: 讲师让我们找出一个维修团队无法直接控制的「关键依赖项」。

words.enDefinition: a component whose failure can stop the operation that relies on it

examples.en: The class identified one shared label printer as a single point of failure for the dispatch desk.
examples.zh: 同学们发现，发货台只靠一台共用标签打印机，存在「单点故障隐患」。

examples.en: Having only one person trained to update the bookings created a single point of failure.
examples.zh: 只有一人受过更新预约的培训，造成了「单点故障隐患」。

collocations: identify a single point of failure
remove a single point of failure
avoid creating a single point of failure

words.enDefinition: an activity identified as especially important to restore early

examples.en: The group named equipment returns as the first recovery priority for the campus loan desk.
examples.zh: 我们把器材归还列为校园借用服务台首要的「恢复优先项」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether collecting existing orders should be a recovery priority before accepting new ones.
examples.zh: 导师问，在接新订单之前，完成现有订单的取货是否该列为「恢复优先项」。

words.enDefinition: the target length of time after a disruption within which a service or function should be restored

examples.en: The case set a recovery time objective of one afternoon for the campus bookings service.
examples.zh: 案例把校园预约服务的「恢复时间目标」定在一个下午之内。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a longer recovery time objective would be acceptable for the newsletter.
examples.zh: 导师问，对简报业务来说，更长的「恢复时间目标」是否可以接受。

words.enDefinition: the point in time to which data must be recoverable after disruption

examples.en: Our recovery point objective allowed for losing no more than two hours of booking records.
examples.zh: 我们的「恢复点目标」最多允许丢失两小时的预约记录。

examples.en: The lecturer used a day's lost order records to explain what a recovery point objective describes.
examples.zh: 讲师以丢失一天的订单记录为例，解释了「恢复点目标」表示什么。

collocations: a recovery point objective for booking data

words.enDefinition: the longest interruption a service can withstand without unacceptable harm

examples.en: The students estimated maximum tolerable downtime for a service that stores equipment for evening collection.
examples.zh: 学生估算了一个为晚间自取保管器材的服务的「最大可容忍停运时间」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why maximum tolerable downtime was shorter for returns than for new bookings.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么归还业务的「最大可容忍停运时间」要比新预约业务更短。

words.enDefinition: the least amount of service an organisation aims to maintain

examples.en: Our case defined a minimum service level of one staffed desk during the move to temporary rooms.
examples.zh: 案例规定，搬到临时场地期间，「最低服务水平」是保留一个有人值守的服务台。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain how the project would meet its minimum service level.
examples.zh: 导师让我们解释，该项目怎样达到「最低服务水平」。

words.enDefinition: a practice activity that tests how essential work would continue

examples.en: During a continuity exercise, the print team tested serving customers from a different campus building.
examples.zh: 在「业务连续性演练」中，打印团队测试了从校园另一栋楼为顾客提供服务。

examples.en: Our continuity exercise checked how quickly the service desk could contact everyone with a booking.
examples.zh: 我们的「业务连续性演练」检查了服务台能多快联系上所有已经预约的人。

words.enDefinition: a different location from which work can temporarily continue

examples.en: The arts centre identified a nearby studio as an alternate site for evening classes.
examples.zh: 艺术中心把附近一间工作室定为晚间课程的「备用场所」。

examples.en: The class checked whether the alternate site had enough storage for tools and customer orders.
examples.zh: 同学们查看了「备用场所」是否有足够空间存放工具和顾客订购的物品。

words.enDefinition: the gradual return of operations in a planned order

examples.en: The case proposed a phased resumption that reopened equipment returns before the new bookings desk.
examples.zh: 案例提出「分阶段恢复」，先恢复器材归还，再恢复接受新预约的柜台。

examples.en: We debated whether phased resumption would help the campus print shop handle its backlog safely.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「分阶段恢复」能否帮助学校打印店稳妥处理积压工作。

words.enDefinition: a business's ability to adapt and recover after difficulties

examples.en: Our lecturer used a supplier closure to illustrate why business resilience mattered to small cafés.
examples.zh: 讲师用一家供应商关门的例子说明，「企业韧性」为什么对小咖啡馆重要。

examples.en: The course case linked business resilience to training several people to handle key tasks.
examples.zh: 课程案例把「企业韧性」与培养多名能承担关键任务的人员联系起来。

words.enDefinition: reliance on one person for essential knowledge or work

examples.en: The class case showed key-person dependency because only the founder knew how to contact suppliers.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例中，只有创始人知道如何联系供应商，体现了「关键人员依赖」。

examples.en: We discussed how the workshop could reduce key-person dependency before the student manager graduated.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了工作坊怎样在学生经理毕业前减少「关键人员依赖」。

words.enDefinition: preparing people in advance to take over important roles

examples.en: Succession planning helped the student enterprise prepare a new manager before the current one graduated.
examples.zh: 「继任规划」帮助学生企业在现任经理毕业前，为下一任经理做好上岗准备。

examples.en: The lecturer asked why succession planning was important for a student cooperative that changed officers annually.
examples.zh: 讲师问，对每年更换负责人的学生合作社来说，「继任规划」为什么重要。

words.enDefinition: a trading organisation whose main aim is social or environmental benefit

examples.en: The class studied a social enterprise that sold repaired bicycles and provided training to local volunteers.
examples.zh: 我们研究了一家「社会企业」，它出售翻新自行车，也为当地志愿者提供培训。

examples.en: Our report asked how the social enterprise would keep its workshops affordable over the summer.
examples.zh: 我们的报告探讨，这家「社会企业」怎样让暑期工作坊保持实惠。

words.enDefinition: starting and developing ventures to address social or environmental problems

examples.en: The social entrepreneurship elective explored how student teams could build businesses around local needs.
examples.zh: 「社会创业」选修课探讨学生团队如何围绕本地需求创办企业。

examples.en: Our social entrepreneurship project compared two ways to provide affordable access to shared tools.
examples.zh: 我们的「社会创业」项目比较了两种让人们以实惠价格使用共享工具的做法。

words.enDefinition: the sector of organisations such as cooperatives, mutuals and social enterprises that pursue social or member benefits through economic activity

examples.en: The lecturer introduced the social economy through examples of cooperatives and community businesses near campus.
examples.zh: 讲师用校园附近的合作社和社区企业举例，介绍「社会经济部门」。

examples.en: Our group discussed how the social economy could support rural communities with few local services.
examples.zh: 我们小组讨论了「社会经济部门」怎样支持当地服务较少的乡村社区。

words.enDefinition: a central purpose to benefit a community or address a problem

examples.en: The repair service's social mission was to make used equipment accessible to more local students.
examples.zh: 维修服务的「社会使命」是让更多本地学生用上二手器材。

examples.en: Potential funding partners asked how the proposed expansion would support the venture's social mission.
examples.zh: 潜在资助方问，拟议的扩张会怎样支持该项目的「社会使命」。

collocations: stay true to the social mission

words.enDefinition: a short statement explaining an organisation's central purpose

examples.en: The team revised its mission statement after members disagreed about who the bookshop should serve.
examples.zh: 成员对书店该服务谁意见不一，团队随后修改了「使命宣言」。

examples.en: In class, we compared the workshop's mission statement with the projects it actually funded.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将工作坊的「使命宣言」与它实际资助的项目作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a statement describing the future an organisation hopes to create

examples.en: The group's vision statement imagined a campus where every student could borrow basic tools.
examples.zh: 小组的「愿景宣言」描绘了一个每个学生都能借到基本工具的校园。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to shorten the vision statement so people could remember it easily.
examples.zh: 导师请我们缩短「愿景宣言」，让大家更容易记住。

words.enDefinition: a gradual move away from an organisation's stated purpose

examples.en: Members worried about mission drift as the cooperative began serving fewer students on tight budgets.
examples.zh: 得到合作社服务的经济拮据学生越来越少，成员开始担心出现「使命偏离」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether taking private bookings might lead to mission drift in the community workshop.
examples.zh: 讲师问，接受私人预约会不会使社区工作坊出现「使命偏离」。

words.enDefinition: a business jointly owned and democratically controlled by its members

examples.en: Our class compared a cooperative enterprise owned by its users with a shop owned by one family.
examples.zh: 我们班把一家由用户共同拥有的「合作社」与一家家族商店作了比较。

examples.en: The case described how members of a cooperative enterprise decided what to do with a surplus.
examples.zh: 案例描述了「合作社」的成员如何决定怎样使用盈余。

words.enDefinition: a cooperative owned and democratically controlled by its workers

examples.en: A worker cooperative took over the repair business in the case after the founder retired.
examples.zh: 案例中，创始人退休后，一家「工人合作社」接手了维修业务。

examples.en: The students discussed how a worker cooperative might let staff share responsibility for new equipment purchases.
examples.zh: 学生讨论了「工人合作社」怎样让员工共同承担采购新设备的责任。

words.enDefinition: a voting rule giving each member an equal vote

examples.en: The student cooperative used one member, one vote when deciding whether to open a second workshop.
examples.zh: 学生合作社决定是否增开一个工作坊时，采用「一人一票」规则。

examples.en: Our tutor contrasted one member, one vote with voting rights tied to the number of shares.
examples.zh: 导师把「一人一票」和按持股数量分配表决权的做法作了比较。

collocations: a one member, one vote rule
the principle of one member, one vote

words.enDefinition: joint ownership of an organisation by the people who belong to it

examples.en: The case described how member ownership gave students a shared stake in the equipment business.
examples.zh: 案例描述了「成员共同所有」如何使学生在设备经营项目中拥有共同权益。

examples.en: Our lecturer compared member ownership with a model that let outside investors hold the entire business.
examples.zh: 讲师将「成员共同所有」与让外部投资者持有整个企业的模式作了比较。

collocations: a model based on member ownership

words.enDefinition: an approach considering social, environmental, and financial performance together

examples.en: The class used the triple bottom line to compare two plans for refurbishing campus furniture.
examples.zh: 同学们用「三重底线」比较了两项校园家具翻新方案。

examples.en: The team presented its triple bottom line results using figures on waste, access, and costs.
examples.zh: 团队用废弃物数量、服务可及性和成本的数据汇报了「三重底线」成果。

words.enDefinition: systematic assessment of the changes an activity helps produce

examples.en: The lecturer used impact measurement to examine whether affordable repairs helped students keep using their bicycles.
examples.zh: 讲师用「影响评估」考察实惠的维修有没有帮助学生继续使用原来的自行车。

examples.en: Our class discussed impact measurement before choosing indicators for the community equipment library.
examples.zh: 我们班先讨论了「影响评估」，然后为社区器材借用中心选择指标。

words.enDefinition: communicating evidence about changes an organisation helps bring about

examples.en: The venture improved its impact reporting by sharing data on who used the repair workshops.
examples.zh: 该项目分享了哪些人使用维修工作坊的数据，改进了「影响报告」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether impact reporting should include the things that had not improved yet.
examples.zh: 导师问，「影响报告」是否应该涵盖那些尚未改善的方面。

words.enDefinition: to use excess income to support future work

examples.en: The cooperative chose to reinvest the surplus in tools that members could borrow from the workshop.
examples.zh: 合作社选择「将盈余再投入」，购置成员可以从工作坊借用的工具。

examples.en: The course case asked how the venture could reinvest the surplus while keeping repairs affordable.
examples.zh: 课程案例问，项目怎样在维持维修价格实惠的同时「将盈余再投入」。

collocations: reinvest the surplus in the community

words.enDefinition: comments from people a programme or organisation aims to help

examples.en: The student team used beneficiary feedback to change the hours of its free repair workshops.
examples.zh: 学生团队根据「受益者反馈」调整了免费维修工作坊的开放时间。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked what beneficiary feedback suggested about access to the community tool library.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「受益者反馈」反映出社区工具借用中心在服务可及性上有哪些情况。
